Figure 47: (Top Row): Measured transient charge rate and (Bottom Row): Measured transient heat transfer fluid temperature and bulk sulfur temperature during charge Figure 47 illustrates the charge rate, heat transfer fluid (HTF) inlet temperature into the sulfur TES, and bulk temperature variation for the three thermal cyclic experimental runs completed during this reporting period. The peak charge rate measured was 80 kW. A controlled ramp-up and ramp-down of the heater power was conducted during the charge runs to mimic a solar profile. Figure 48 displays the discharge rate, HTF exit temperature from the sulfur TES, and bulk temperature variation during those experimental runs. During discharge, the pump speed was regulated to maintain the discharge rate between 25–35 kW, in alignment with the EOP-B target for a 14-hour discharge duration. This highlights the system's ability to deliver steady heat output over extended durations. Also, the HTF exit temperature from the TES remained above 205°C (±5°C) throughout the discharge process. Maintaining the HTF exit temperature above 205°C while ensuring a near- constant discharge rate demonstrates the sulfur TES system's capability to reliably meet industrial process heat demands above 200°C. . Figure 48: (Top Row): Measured transient discharge rate and (Bottom Row): Measured transient heat transfer fluid temperature and bulk sulfur temperature during discharge. A charge-discharge thermal cycle was selected such that the bulk sulfur temperature at the start of the charge closely matched the bulk sulfur temperature at the end of discharge. This method ensured that the internal energy of the system at the start and end of the cycle was approximately the same, thereby minimizing errors in the energy balance and enabling an accurate round-trip efficiency calculation. The discharge and charge duration for each cycle is 14 hours and 8.7 to 8.8 hours, respectively, with a total cycle time of approximately 23 hours. The average round trip thermal efficiency of sulfur TES for the three cycles illustrated in Figures 47 and 48 was calculated to be 83.6% with the highest of 85%. Figure 49 illustrates the comparison of charge and discharge times across the ten thermal cycles. The figure highlights system performance in achieving two critical targets: (a) Discharge time > 14 hours and (b) Charge time < 10 hours. Both charge and discharge times remained consistent across all runs, reflecting reliable operation and repeatable performance of the sulfur TES system.
